market.summary: Market sentiment is cautious as Iran's attack on a US warship in the Strait of Hormuz pushed S&P 500 futures down 0.4% pre-bell, though strong tech earnings and AI-driven momentum continue to underpin resilience with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq fresh off record closes.
key_drivers: Iran attack on US warship in Hormuz drops S&P 500 futures 0.4%, Nasdaq 0.5%
Tech earnings and AI momentum providing market resilience per Morgan Stanley
AI chipmakers driving Asian stocks back to all-time highs despite initial geopolitical shock
Fed chair transition uncertainty as Warsh raises questions on monetary policy independence

Technology.summary: AI chipmakers drove Asian stocks to record highs, Morgan Stanley sees tech earnings eclipsing geopolitical fears, and Cerebras targets a $3.5B IPO at $24.5B valuation — partially offset by Microsoft lagging peers on AI spending concerns.

Healthcare.summary: A Deloitte report flags a 'bubble effect' as GLP-1/obesity assets now represent 25% of late-stage pharma pipeline while oncology's share has slipped to 20%, raising concentration risk concerns for the sector.

Energy.summary: Oil prices jumped after Iran's navy halted a US warship in the Strait of Hormuz, providing a near-term positive price catalyst for energy stocks that offsets the prior OPEC+ supply increase headwind.

Financials.summary: Bitcoin breaking $80,000 boosted crypto-exposed stocks like Coinbase and Strategy, though Kevin Warsh's unconventional stance on Fed independence is introducing uncertainty into the monetary policy outlook.

Consumer Discretionary.summary: Amazon made a significant strategic move positive for retail sector outlook, while the GameStop-eBay takeover bid injects speculative activity into e-commerce.

Industrials.summary: Airlines are tackling a fuel cost surge from Middle East tensions with price hikes and outlook cuts, compounding the existing warning signs flagged for industrials stocks.

AMD.summary: AMD surged 74% in April and is up 68.4% YTD, ranking as the 21st-best S&P 500 performer, driven by its position as an AI chip leader.

AAPL.summary: Apple is explicitly cited as being in a buy zone as the S&P 500 and Nasdaq trade at all-time highs following strong Big Tech earnings.

AVGO.summary: Broadcom is named alongside Apple as being in a buy zone, benefiting from the strong Big Tech AI earnings cycle.

AMZN.summary: Amazon made a significant strategic move with positive implications for the broader retail sector, reinforcing its competitive position.

META.summary: Cathie Wood's Ark Invest purchased $28.7 million of Meta after a 9% post-earnings decline, signaling institutional buy-the-dip conviction.

BRK.B.summary: New CEO Greg Abel earned broadly positive reviews from Berkshire shareholders at his first annual meeting, ruling out a breakup and emphasizing continuity with Buffett's legacy.

MSFT.summary: Microsoft is described as lagging its megacap peers as investors question its AI capital expenditure plans, with analyst commentary calling it 'a mess' relative to the Magnificent Seven.
